title: The Galois group conjecture for the polynomial Q_n
statement:
Let $n\geq 2$, let $Q_n$ be the polynomial studied in the paper, and write

$$
D_{0,n}=\operatorname{Disc}(Q_n).
$$

For a polynomial with rational coefficients, let $\operatorname{Gal}(Q_n)$ denote its Galois group and let $A_n$ and $S_n$ be the alternating and symmetric groups, respectively. **Galois group conjecture.** For integers $n\geq 2$,

$$
\operatorname{Gal}(Q_n)=\begin{cases}
A_n & \text{if $D_{0,n}$ is a square};\\
S_n & \text{if $D_{0,n}$ is not a square}.
\end{cases}
$$

The conjecture refines the general fact that a square discriminant forces the Galois group to be contained in an alternating group. It is supported by computations, but no resolution is given here.
references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (1994–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1909.03541](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.03541), [arXiv:math/9411238](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9411238).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.11222

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2019).
source_name: Karl Dilcher and Maciej Ulas, “Arithmetic properties of polynomial solutions of the Diophantine equation P(x)x^n+1+Q(x)(x+1)^n+1=1”, arXiv:1909.11222 (2019).
